classification.difficultyReason: Partition each supplied graph into quarter-circle, triangle and rectangle regions and combine their areas.

spec.description: Two outer unit quarter-circle arcs joined by straight segments through (2,0). Dashed guides at y=1, x=1 and x=3; half-unit minor ticks; no shading.
spec.mathematics: Quarter-circles centred at (1,0) and (3,0), with triangles on [1,2] and [2,3].
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is visible in every edition; no answer annotations.

answer.worked:
The outer regions are two quarter-circles of radius $1$. The middle regions are two triangles, each with base $1$ and height $1$.
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx&=2\left(\frac{\pi(1)^2}{4}\right)+2\left(\frac12\times1\times1\right)\\&=\frac{\pi}{2}+1.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Concave-up unit quarter-circle arc from (0,0) to (1,1), horizontal segment to (2,1), line to (3,0), and concave-down unit quarter-circle arc to (4,1). Dashed guides at y=1 and x=1,2,4; half-unit minor ticks; no shading.
spec.mathematics: First arc has centre (0,1), and last arc has centre (4,0). The first area is 1−π/4 and the last is π/4.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is visible in every edition; no answer annotations.

answer.worked:
From left to right, the regions are a unit square minus a unit quarter-circle, a unit square, a triangle, and a unit quarter-circle.
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx&=\left(1-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+1+\frac12\times1\times1+\frac{\pi}{4}\\&=\frac52\\&=2.5.\end{align*}$$
